Dhyan Shirashyad

Aspiring aerospace design engineer · Mechanical Engineering, Ohlone College

Executive Summary

I’m a mechanical engineering student at Ohlone College, and my goal is to become an aerospace design engineer working on structures and mechanisms. This career usually requires a bachelor’s degree,1 so I’m on a transfer pathway to a UC, planned for Spring 2029. This fall I’m taking calculus and Intro to Engineering, and my plan adds physics, Statics, Dynamics, Materials, Circuit Analysis, MATLAB, and C++.

Outside class, I’m secretary and a founding member of my college’s aerospace and rocketry club, and I’m working on rocketry for competition while helping manage the club. I’m also a core chassis team engineer for the first NorCal community college Formula SAE team, and I’ve built an indoor delivery robot and an AI vision project at my first hackathon. I’m drawn to NASA’s Research and Technology and Human Spaceflight directorates,2 especially lunar rover and propulsion work like the projects NASA Force hires for.3

Next, I plan to finish my engineering degree, learn simulation tools like Ansys and MATLAB, and apply for NASA OSTEM internships.4 Along the way, I’ll keep building hands-on projects, compete with my club’s rocket, and look for research or internship experience before I transfer. Long term, I want to work as an early-career aerospace engineer at NASA or in the aerospace industry, and later earn my engineering license.

Experiences & Projects

Indoor Delivery Robot

STEM Summer Bridge · 2026

Task: build a delivery robot for a school building, where GPS doesn’t work. Action: I coded Python navigation on a Raspberry Pi using a map from real measurements, shortest-path routing, gyro turns, and ultrasonic obstacle avoidance. Result: a complete autonomous indoor navigation program.

NASA rovers on the Moon and Mars can’t use GPS either, so they rely on maps, path planning, and obstacle avoidance. NASA Force hires for lunar rover operations,3 which is this same navigation problem at a larger scale.

View the project presentation slides

Core Chassis Engineer, Formula SAE

Ohlone College Formula SAE team · Oct 2026 – present

Task: design a rules-compliant Formula SAE chassis. Action: as core chassis engineer for the first NorCal community college FSAE team, I check the Onshape frame against rules and design control arms, mounts, uprights, and tubing. Result: a rules-checked model and designed parts; not built yet.

Aerospace structures engineers also design to strict requirements and then verify them. Design engineer is one of the job titles O*NET lists for aerospace engineers.1 This builds the CAD and requirements skills I would use on flight or lunar hardware.

“Kamikaze” Hackathon Project

ExecuTorch Hackathon, IoT Track · Oct 17–18, 2026

Task: build a working project in an 18-hour hackathon with my first-year team. Action: we built Kamikaze, a VENTUNO Q camera system that recognizes phones and cans on the device, with AI tools helping write code; I helped debug and test. Result: live recognition with a 3D dashboard and LEDs.

NASA’s Research and Technology directorate develops new space technology.2 Running AI vision on the device itself, not a remote computer, matters for machines that can’t count on a fast link to Earth. It also built my teamwork and troubleshooting skills.
